newsitem.title: USA: US, EU meat talks continue, key isssues unsettled.
newsitem.headline: US, EU meat talks continue, key isssues unsettled.

text.p: U.S. and European negotiators had scheduled a short meeting Thursday morning to discuss still unresolved issues in a dispute over meat imports, but sources said that little progress has been made this week in the frustrating trade talks.
"The big issue is still there...poultry is still undecided," said EU spokesperson Ella Krucoff.

Negotiators ended talks Wednesday at around 2000 EDT/2400 GMT, and were set to meet for another two hours Thursday morning. EU officials were expected to depart Washington Thursday afternoon, and it appeared likely that they would be leaving without an agreement in hand.
"Apparently no progress was made yesterday...and officials are skeptical they will do anything today," said a source close to the talks. "They're not going to get anything resolved this morning."
Informed sources said Wednesday that the talks would move to Brussels next week if no agreement was reached, but those plans appeared not to be firm at this point.

U.S. and EU officials have been meeting this week in a last-ditch effort to resolve a fight over meat import inspection regulations that threatens to disrupt the trade of hundreds of millions of dollars worth of poultry and meat shipments.

Officials have been trying to reach an agreement in the so-called veterinary equivalency talks by April 15 when Washington has said it will remove over 100 poultry and meat processing plants from its list of approved exporters.
EU on April 1 adopted new rules that have halted the shipment of U.S. poultry to Europe.
One of the sticking points has been disagreement over decontamination procedures used by U.S. and EU poultry processors.

The dispute threatens to halt the trade of up to $100 million worth of U.S. poultry and dairy exports to Europe and some $300 million worth of EU meat imports to the U.S., mostly pork products from Denmark and Italian hams.
